query: For Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 initially in a high-temperature BCC state, the factors governing its phase stability during cooling and subsequent thermal exposure are not understood well enough to account for the range of phases that may appear. What single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain this behavior and why? Define a controlled comparison and baseline, predicted observations relative to that baseline, the conditions under which the hypothesis should and should not apply, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification result.

generation.hypothesis: In Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7, the appearance or absence of σ-phase on cooling from the single–phase high-temperature BCC (A2) field is controlled by whether Cr-rich short-range–ordered (SRO) clusters form in the parent BCC matrix while it traverses the 1000 – 800 °C interval; these clusters nucleate σ during subsequent cooling or ageing. If the alloy is quenched fast enough to suppress the development of Cr-rich SRO, σ cannot nucleate and the alloy instead retains a mixture of A2/B2 that later decomposes to B2+FCC during isothermal exposure. Thus, “Cr-SRO formation during the 1000–800 °C dwell” is the single rate-controlling step that governs the later phase selection.
generation.material_initial_state: Homogeneous single–phase BCC (A2) solid solution at 1150 °C, grain size ≈50 µm, no pre-existing second phases.
generation.intervention: Cooling trajectory through 1000 – 800 °C: (a) slow furnace cool (≈1 °C s⁻¹) long enough to allow Cr diffusion vs. (b) water quench (>100 °C s⁻¹) that minimises diffusion time in this window.
generation.conditions: Solutionise 30 min at 1150 °C (A2 single phase), then apply the two cooling paths; after reaching room temperature, age both conditions 24 h at 700 °C in Ar atmosphere.
generation.structural_mediator: Extent of Cr-rich SRO in the as-cooled BCC, quantified by the Warren–Cowley parameter or diffuse neutron/X-ray scattering intensity at the <½½½> positions.
generation.mechanism: Slow cooling permits bulk Cr diffusion (D_Cr ≈10⁻¹⁶ m² s⁻¹ at 900 °C) so that attractive Cr–Cr interactions (negative ∆H_mix(Cr-Cr) with Co/Fe/Ni, positive with Al) drive the formation of nanometre-scale Cr-rich SRO domains. These act as chemically compatible embryos for the topologically close-packed σ phase, lowering its nucleation barrier. Rapid quenching freezes a more random distribution (low SRO); without Cr-rich nuclei, σ nucleation during later ageing is slow and the system follows the lower-barrier spinodal pathway toward B2 ordering plus FCC precipitation.
generation.predicted_outcome: After the 24 h /700 °C age, the slow-cooled material will contain >10 vol % σ phase (identified by its tetragonal P42/mnm structure, Cr-rich composition) whereas the quenched material will show <1 vol % σ but prominent B2-ordered precipitates and emerging FCC (CoFeNi-rich) colonies. The as-cooled SRO signal (pre-ageing) will be at least twice as strong in the slow-cooled sample.
generation.baseline: Water-quenched specimen: low Cr-SRO, negligible σ after 24 h /700 °C ageing, dominant B2+incipient FCC.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis should hold for cooling/ageing sequences that pass through 1000–800 °C where Cr diffusion is significant. At temperatures ≥1050 °C (no SRO) or ≤600 °C (negligible Cr mobility) σ should not form regardless of prior cooling rate. Alloy chemistries with ≤25 at.% Cr should also fall outside the σ-forming regime.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of SRO needed to trigger σ is not precisely known; other elements (Al-driven B2 ordering) may partly mask the effect, introducing scatter in σ fractions.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare three identical 10-g buttons of Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7. Solution-treat all at 1150 °C/30 min. Cool one by furnace (1 °C s⁻¹), one by salt-bath quench (20 °C s⁻¹), one by water quench (>100 °C s⁻¹). Characterise as-cooled SRO using synchrotron diffuse scattering and atom probe tomography. Then age all at 700 °C/24 h and quantify phase fractions by synchrotron XRD and EBSD.
measurements: Diffuse scattering intensity at <½½½> positions (Cr-SRO indicator)
Volume fraction of σ by Rietveld refinement of XRD
Fraction of FCC by EBSD phase mapping
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If (i) the quenched sample shows σ ≥5 vol % after ageing OR (ii) furnace-cooled sample shows <5 vol % σ while having SRO level comparable (within 20 %) to the quenched sample, then the hypothesis is falsified.
